## school-mode

The native app has a real shared School mode runtime. It uses a bounded version-1 record in %LOCALAPPDATA%/DingDing/SharedPresentation/school-mode-v1.json, guarded by a lock-file compare-and-swap, with a 500 ms poll plus a filesystem watcher. It fails closed until the record is read. The unlock credential lives in the OS vault under a shared account with an attempt budget. A Preferences control can rename the mode, set or replace the credential, enable it, and unlock-and-disable it, and includes the honest 'not a security boundary' disclosure. While the mode is on, suppression is applied to the language mode, funny levels, bilingual decorator, personal vocabulary, the Cantonese narrator, settings teleport, and palette preference rows. Several required parts are missing. Dim-sum surfaces are not suppressed: changelog code names, the release splash art, the surprise display path, and the palette document entries for codenames and splash art. The offline documentation viewer still offers Cantonese and bilingual articles and dim-sum articles, and its bundled text reveals the shipped name. Open surfaces (the modal Preferences, palette, docs, changelog) are not rebuilt live; most suppression is decided once, when the dialog is built. There is no passkey choice. Status copy uses generic wording instead of the chosen name. The control's strings are not in the Cantonese catalogue. The emoji switch is suppressed even though the contract does not list it. The School unlock lockout has no unlock ladder. The local-capability bridge registers no school.state or school.manage handlers. The public site has no School mode. There is no user-facing article and no .yue_HK twin. Only service-level tests and no built-app captures exist.

## adhd-modes

The native Windows app ships no attention modes. src/slic3r/GUI/PersonalModes/AttentionModes.hpp is a header-only service with five default-off modes, idle and snooze timing, and a persistence callback. Its only consumer is tests/personal_modes/personal_modes_tests.cpp, so in the product it is dead code. No GUI_App owner, Preferences section, persisted keys, workspace callbacks, palette entries, export, or Cantonese copy exist, and docs/features/personal-modes/integration.md lists all of this as unchecked. The public site has a real per-visitor implementation in ui-md3/site/attention.js: five independent default-off switches, an emphasized current item, low stimulation with CSS and notification filtering, a session and since-change clock in the header, a persisted next action, and a momentum reminder with a 30-minute 'Not now'. It has English and Cantonese copy, settings search, and 7 source tests. On the site, momentum reminders are silently suppressed whenever low stimulation is on, so those two modes are not independent. Palette registration, local history, export, School interaction, and real browser captures are documented as unfinished. Embedded WebView2 pages carry nothing.

## scheduled-settings

Main compiles and runs two independent scheduled-settings engines at the same time, with separate stores, different precedence, and conflicting semantics. Engine A (src/slic3r/GUI/Schedule, Preferences > Schedules) stores rules in AppConfig 'scheduled_settings' and supports 9 keys with list-order precedence. It applies values by writing them permanently into AppConfig base settings and keeps a separate captured-base map. It reads the 'live' value through AppConfig::get, which returns School-suppressed or overlay values, so it can capture and later permanently write a suppressed or scheduled value as the user's base. It reads the Home Assistant token from plaintext 'ha_token' in the config and has no private-address or DNS-rebinding protection. Its language changes only take effect after restart, and its rule editor offers Cantonese, bilingual and funny-level values even under School mode. Engine B (libslic3r/ScheduledSettings plus FeatureServices::ScheduledPreferences, File > Scheduled settings) is the stronger design: a strict schema, priority then order, a nonpersistent EffectivePreferences overlay, a vault-stored Home Assistant token, DNS-pinned curl with no redirects and bounded size and time, a history snapshot, a timezone list, and School-aware key filtering. However, its 'Add rule' seeds the unregistered key 'theme', so a new rule can never validate or save. Its strings bypass the catalogue (the translate callback drops the inline Cantonese). Its failure notice carries no recovery action and fires only for two states. It uses raw wx controls. Neither engine covers every appearance or customization value (element styles, logo, font weight and others). Neither is in Export everything. Engine B's tests are not in CTest, and Engine A has no tests. The two documentation articles contradict each other, and the Engine B README has no Cantonese twin. The public site has a local-only rule engine with 13 source tests; its API and Home Assistant sources are shown as unavailable.

## language

The three baseline modes are implemented and persisted under the AppConfig key 'language' (en, yue_HK, bilingual_en_yue_HK). They fall back to English, and changing the mode recreates the GUI. A bilingual decorator pairs labels across wx widgets, ImGui text and notifications. Embedded web pages resolve all three modes through resources/web/data/text.js (282 of 282 keys, 4 empty). The yue_HK catalogue covers about 98.7% of the current POT (7757 of 7860). Three things are missing. First, the xgettext source list and POT are stale: newer surfaces such as the Ollama suite, local converter, settings drafts, offline documentation, Status Hub, the scheduled-settings panel and the dim sum card are not extracted, and 103 POT strings (narrator, School mode, export, Status Hub) have no Cantonese, so Cantonese mode shows English there. Second, a scheduled language change only applies to windows created after it. Third, the export allowlist drops the yue_HK and bilingual modes. Native compilation and runtime of the three modes on current main are unverified. Palette registration for every language and voice setting is tracked here for all families.

## funny-emoji

Preferences > General has two independent persisted sliders (funny_level_en and funny_level_yue, default 5, clamped 1-5) that update the language service live. It also has a persisted 'Show emojis in dialogs and message boxes' switch. A one-time first-run disclosure exists, and unit tests cover clamping, parsing and the emoji guard on action labels. The sliders are mostly unwired. The ladder table holds only 9 source strings, and the legacy _L()/_u8L() path (LanguageModeService::finish) never consults it. 'Unsaved Changes', 'Slicing complete', 'Export successfully.' and 'Model file downloaded.' therefore render the same at every level. Only the few translate_mode() call sites change: the language-restart dialog, the slider labels, the disclosure and the smart-home dialog. The ladders and the dim sum lines are hard-coded in C++ rather than kept in catalogue resources. There is no per-slider reset. The disclosure does not mention the default of 5 or reset. The emoji decorates only MsgDialog-family headlines; other MD3Dialog dialogs, 27 raw wxMessageBox calls, ImGui popups and embedded web dialogs get none. The emoji switch is hidden in School mode, although the contract does not list it for suppression. The documentation still states a default of 2. Palette registration is tracked under the language family.

## personal-vocabulary

Preferences (Appearance page) always shows a Personal vocabulary box, except under School mode. It has Load/Replace JSON, a Clear button, a semantic wxFileDialog picker, and localized no-file, loaded and invalid status text. The parser enforces schema version 1, a 1 MiB limit, depth 3, 2048 entries and 512-byte strings. It rejects duplicate and unsafe keys and unknown fields, and never applies a rejected file partially. The validated cache is written atomically to a private local app-data folder that stores no source path. Replacements are applied only at display adapters (Label painting, Button including its accessible name, DropDown, MD3Menu, canvas menu labels, SurfaceRegistry), and the profile export skips the cache path. Five things are missing. The palette has no vocabulary entries. Label accessible names, native wx controls, tooltips, window titles, notifications and general ImGui text bypass the transform. Embedded WebView2 pages have neither the control nor the transform. Exports and history views do not say that vocabulary data was omitted. Tests cover only parsing and bounds. Palette registration is tracked under the language family.

## narration

The narrator is off by default (narrator_enabled=false) and uses a SAPI late-bound backend. A completion-driven serialized queue speaks English then Cantonese for 'Both', applies a 20-second per-category cooldown, replaces queued lines of the same category, and lets errors bypass the cooldown. It yields to a screen reader (SPI_GETSCREENREADER, polled each second), has a quiet toggle, and shuts down cleanly. Preferences > Other has separate English and Cantonese voice pickers with an Automatic default, stable SAPI token IDs, retained missing selections, an effective-voice status line, per-language rate and pitch from -10 to 10, re-enumeration every 2 seconds, an external-mirror label and palette entries. Seven gaps remain. Only printer state and error changes plus the filament-scanner preview are narrated; slicing, export, update and app error events are not. SAPI-only enumeration misses the OneCore and natural voices where Hong Kong Cantonese voices normally live. Narrator settings copy has no Cantonese translation. Windows quiet hours are not respected. Tone ignores the funny level because narration lines have no ladders. Legacy say() and say_now() follow the interface language. The narration article has no Cantonese twin, and there are no tests for rate and pitch bounds, missing synthesis or every language mode.

## display-name

Preferences > Appearance offers a persisted rename (AppConfig app_display_name, 1-40 code points, no control characters). It has inline validation and provenance, a one-click 'Reset to shipped name', and an explanation that the data folder, installer, updater, logs and diagnostics keep the shipped name. GUI_App::set_app_display_name broadcasts EVT_APP_DISPLAY_NAME_CHANGED, so the title bar, window title, About and MsgDialog captions update live. Identity stays on compile-time constants and is guarded by tests/app_display_name. A scheduled rule can set the name through the scheduler's base and override store. Gaps: about 44 native UI strings and 126 embedded web strings still introduce the app as 'Bambu Studio' (notifications, Preferences rows, the funny-level caption, home page and dialogs). Renames and resets are not recorded as append-only commits in an app-local history behind the password-protected manager; IdentityHistory has a Renamed action, but nothing feeds it and no restore dispatcher is registered. There are no restart or live-surface tests. Palette registration is tracked under the language family.

## dim-sum

The native startup surprise is missing at runtime. DimSumSurprise.cpp and DimSumSurpriseModel.hpp are compiled and well built: a fresh 10% draw, a once-per-process guard, an eligibility matrix, a public-catalog-only source, an app-data cache that records source URL, ETag revision and fetch time, a non-focus popup, reduced-motion and quiet handling, and bilingual names and alt text. However, commit d2804f1e2 ('Remove unsolicited workflow prompts') removed the only call to DimSumSurprise::maybe_show_after_startup. scripts/check-quiet-prompts.mjs (CTest quiet_prompt_source_contract) now fails if the call returns, and the docs mark the feature retired, which contradicts 'cannot be opted out of'. A static_assert in DimSumSurprise.cpp:5 requires DimSum::FUNNY_LEVEL_DEFAULT to equal I18N::FUNNY_LEVEL_DEFAULT, but they are 2 and 5. That is a probable compile failure, and tests/dim_sum requires 5. The card does not check School mode, an update in progress, or announce itself to screen readers. Release code names come from a static inline roster in build_all.yml with invented style-and-dish combinations rather than catalog name.en/name.zhHant entries. They have no published-photo check or used-once ledger, and they are not shown in About or the in-app changelog. CI-generated dim sum splash art also remains. The Pages site has a working surprise from public catalog-v1 assets.

## material-design

The native shell is frameless, with a custom Material title bar. A shared native MD3 kit (tokens, dialog caption, menus, scrollbars, kit controls) replaced stock wx controls, and source guards refuse stock controls. Preferences has persisted, live controls for theme, density, accent seed, font family, three-step text size and motion. Parts of the contract are not met. The token layer is a custom kit, not the full M3 (Expressive) scheme: there are 25 colour roles, no secondary/tertiary/fixed families, the seed derives only 6 tonal roles, the type ramp is custom, there is no spring motion and no state-layer tokens. No component registry with provenance exists. Embedded WebView2 pages use jQuery/Shoelace/Radix/Tailwind and receive only dark/light, never accent, density, font or motion. There is no global font-weight control, and the appearance rows have no explanation or provenance lines. Design-reference parity is blocked: there is no reference viewer, no deterministic built-app route and no captures or diffs, and the manifest records referenceViewerStatus=missing and parityStatus=blocked. Parity-register rows are 'done (source)' with captures pending.

## motion

A shared interruptible animator exists (MD3::Motion::Anim) with weak-owner settling, duration tokens and standard/emphasized easing. A persisted 'Interface motion' preference (system/reduced) is OR-ed with the Windows client-area-animation setting and can be scheduled. Several slices are implemented in source: state-colour interpolation, tab underline, checkbox and slider emphasis, menu, dialog and palette entrances, canvas tooltip rail, and notification and progress reduced-motion. The repository's own inventory calls this a foundation. Page-content transitions (Notebook/Tabbook DoShowPage) and exit transitions are missing. There is no M3 Expressive spring scheme. Several animators bypass the shared policy: AnimaIcon, BaseTransparentDPIFrame, and DimSumSurprise, which reads only the OS setting. The low-stimulation attention mode is a dead header that never feeds reduced(). Embedded pages never receive the app preference. No installed temporal evidence exists.

## appearance-editor

A per-element style registry exists: 16 scalar properties, id inheritance, shipped and user presets, versioned JSON with unknown-key preservation, import/export, and per-property, per-element and global reset. A non-modal anchored editor card has Typography, Colours, Shape and Presets sections, font and preset search with the regex SearchField, and focus return. Entry points are the MD3 context-menu auto item, Shift+right-click, Ctrl+Shift+E, palette entries and tab-strip menu items. In practice few paint paths read the registry: MD3Menu rows, the top bar, Preferences row labels and the editor's own chrome. Generic SurfaceRegistry adoption only sets wx font and colours, which owner-drawn kit widgets ignore. The tab, group and strip editors write 'tab:', 'group:' and 'tabstrip:' ids that no renderer consumes, and the article still describes ProjectTabBar wiring that no longer exists. Auto-adopted elements get no right-click menu. There is no state dimension, no layered or Photoshop-depth editing, and no Word-depth rich-text renderer. Undo/redo, history, copy/paste style, property search, provenance lines, scheduled presets and web-page or canvas coverage are all missing.

## color-picker

MD3ColorPickerDialog is a genuine continuous picker. It has an SV field and hue strip that both respond to the keyboard, a tonal ladder, optional recent colours, alpha, hex, and a 16-notation translator (named, HEX/HEX8, RGB/RGBA, HSL/HSLA, HSV, HWB, XYZ, LAB, LCH, OKLab, OKLCH, CMYK) with copy buttons. It also parses any notation and shows the gamut, a clipping warning and WCAG contrast. Most native colour controls use it. Gaps: there is no animated-rainbow sentinel anywhere in the codebase. The scheduled-settings panel still uses the native wxColourPickerCtrl. Embedded pages and the Pages site use input type=color. There is no swatch grid, no user custom-colour set and no picker search with a regex builder. The dialog is modal, not anchored, and is not explicitly customizable by the appearance system. Accessibility values for the 2D field, and dialog-level tests, are missing.

## overlay-panels

The shared MD3Menu paints its own surface. It places itself within the display work area, scrolls internally when it does not fit, and shows a right-aligned caption-sized shortcut column that it exposes to assistive technology through GetKeyboardShortcut. ## element-locks

The building blocks exist, but nothing in the app can actually be locked. The libslic3r LocalSecurity library has the six ordered policies, PBKDF2 PIN and password verifiers in Windows Credential Manager, TOTP with replay protection, the three unlock durations, Lock again, locked-on-launch, and an in-memory attempt budget (5 tries, then a 30 s wait that doubles up to 900 s). LockWizard is compiled and offers all six policies, the duration choice, the toy-lock disclosure with the exact recovery folder, keypad plus manual PIN entry feeding one validator, and focus return. However, LockWizard::Open and ElementLock are never called outside the unit tests. There is no 'Lock this element...' command, no interception of activation routes, no tab or tab-group locks, no appearance-property locks, no lock list or manager, and no honesty about locked items in search or the palette. ElementLock has no change or remove API. Lock creation records through the password-protected identity history, so it fails until that history is enrolled. The UI copy is not in any i18n catalogue. There are no Pages-site or embedded-web-page locks, and nothing has been run on Windows. The project's own state document marks this family Incomplete for both native and browser.

## support-tickets

The local service and native panel exist and are reachable from File > Local support tickets... (and therefore from the command palette, which indexes the menu bar). Tickets are AES-GCM encrypted under the application-data folder, with the key in the vault. The panel has category, description, a fictional severity, a local id, three advancing stages and a regex search. Removal goes through the two-key gate, the export is prose, and the folder path is shown and copyable. Open application-data folder opens the folder without deleting anything and reports honestly if it cannot be launched. A factual 'nothing is sent anywhere' line is rendered outside the funny-level formatter. Gaps: there is no Help menu route and no lock-setting route. The unlock-prompt link lives in LockWizard, which is never opened. The desk flow is thin: the list shows raw numeric stages, there is no category or severity text, and the 'canned first response' is a single status line. Export is a single prose format with numeric enums. The copy is not in any catalogue, so it has no Cantonese. There is no dedicated article and no yue_HK twin, no Pages-site equivalent, no route, no-network or disclosure-invariance tests, and no Windows runtime proof.

## unlock-ladder

No unlock ladder exists. The only related code is AttemptBudget::clear_wait. It allows at most 3 wait-skips per rolling hour, restores the same 5 attempts that ordinary expiry restores, and leaves escalation untouched, but nothing calls it. There is no dim-sum, sums or whack-a-mole challenge, no trusted grading, no single-use nonce, no expiry, no mole timing or per-mole grading, no School-mode starting-rung function and no UI. Every attempt budget is in-memory, so restarting the app refunds attempts and resets escalation. The skip cap is per budget instance rather than global. Three native lockout surfaces exist without a ladder: the School-mode credential in Preferences, the identity-history password, and the element-lock prompt. A Pages-site lockout will exist once site toy locks are built.

## authenticator

A real local authenticator exists. AuthenticatorStore keeps up to 32 entries in Windows Credential Manager (per-entry stable keys and an index) and requires a current code before adding. It supports rename, group, reorder, remove, restore and a redacted export that states secrets were omitted. TOTP follows RFC 6238 over RFC 4226 with SHA-1/256/512, 6 to 8 digits and any period, verified against all RFC vectors. The panel is reachable from File > Authenticator... and the palette. It has a regex search, a list, a grouped 26pt code, a seconds countdown, copy, a Show next code button, reorder, URI paste and gated removal. Local QR encoding (Nayuki, black on white, quiet zone) plus a revealed manual key exist in the lock wizard. Missing or partial: image, clipboard and camera QR import (hooks are never populated and the ZXing decoder option is OFF); manual entry with parameters (fixed SHA-1/6/30); clock-skew detection (only a disclaimer); a grouped view, editable icons and bulk regroup; selectable code digits with a persistent next-code peek and change-only announcements; and the ornamental-lock notice. Adding an entry fails with a misleading vault error until the separate identity-history password is enrolled. The history retention confirmation hook is unwired, so prune is disabled, and the history manager offers only a password factor. Copy is uncatalogued, docs have no yue_HK twins, the Pages site has no equivalent, the tests are not in ctest, and there is no runtime evidence. Display-name mutation history is not recorded; that belongs to the display-name and local-history families.

## super-confirmation

The native gate is real and broadly matches the contract. SuperConfirmGate is a wx Material surface anchored beside the originating control (centred-modal fallback) with two independently focusable, accessibly named key switches and a slider enabled only when both are on. It has a hazard progress bar, a distinct completion burst, a reduced-motion path, an always-enabled Emergency exit plus Escape, focus return, cancel-only behaviour when space is insufficient, and fully localized yue_HK strings. A pure state machine has 10 Catch2 cases registered in ctest. It gates delete-all, delete preset in Tab, filament slot and plate deletion, bulk actions, export overwrite, Ollama session deletion, and the local-security removals and restore. The Pages site has its own two-key gate in confirmation.js with tests and bilingual docs. Gaps: many irreversible native actions still use Yes/No or OK/Cancel, or nothing: deleting files on the printer, calibration-history deletion with no confirmation at all, preset deletion in CreatePresetsDialog and EditFilamentWebDialog, appearance preset delete and reset-all, scheduled-rule deletion, reset all preferences, clear personal vocabulary and clear AMS filament info. Config profiles export/import still uses a slider-only gate. The embedded filament-manager web page uses the browser's confirm(). There are no widget-level or per-action success/failure tests, and the documented hidden-desktop capture of each gated site is still pending.

## regex-search

A real bounded regex engine runs Boost.Regex in an isolated worker process with size and time limits. The shared SearchField puts a plain-text-default field, a regex toggle and an anchored RegexBuilderPopup on about 30 native surfaces, every MD3 menu and the kit DropDown. ImGui lists use a bridge. The builder offers guided chips, a raw editor, flags, validity, a bounded sample tester with captures, copy and a reference tab. It is not the required workbench: it has no parse tree or token annotation, no capability matrix, no lookaround, named, atomic, possessive or Unicode chips, no replacement preview, test suites, saved snippets or import/export, no match navigation, timing, backtracking-risk diagnostics or trace view. Fields have no per-field history or validation state, and invalid patterns silently match everything. No hand-written per-surface search inventory or negative regression exists. Several settings and properties dialogs, three wxChoice filters, a wxComboBox, a raw camera zoom menu and embedded web page searches lack the builder. One canvas-menu test is orphaned from CMake.

A real WorkflowPrintPanel review page shows its summary, actions and disabled reasons. Slice-and-print continuation is gated by generation (PrintWorkflowState). Registered layout and workflow tests and an English and Cantonese article exist. Gaps: the Print page has no stable TabPosition, so the palette has no 'Go to Print' row or numpad chord. The palette calls Monitor 'Go to Device', and the Print page reuses the Monitor icon. Navigation buttons are not exposed as a tab list with arrow-key roving focus. The article itself records that no built-artifact evidence exists for the navigation or the journeys.

## rich-controls

Some surfaces already show real controls where values appear: Preferences rows, the Plater object table and the palette's Theme, Density, Accent and Narrator rows. ## guided-forms

A few elements follow the contract. The funny-level sliders and the app display-name editor have progressive-disclosure explanations and truthful provenance lines. ## local-history

A real libgit2-backed, append-only history exists for projects (bare repos under data_dir/project_history/v1), a 30-key preferences allowlist, preset/draft saves, printer transitions, and a separate password-protected encrypted identity history for authenticator entries. The Version history dialog browses, compares, labels, restores (recorded as a new revision), bulk-exports and exports the filtered list. It falls short of the contract in several ways. The date filter is plain ISO text with no calendar. The 'action' filter is a hard-coded store-category list with no counts. Revision messages are generic ('Project edit', 'Preferences change'). There is no retention or pruning for project, preferences or preset stores, even though the docs say portable publication blocks until a retention operation runs. Display-name changes and preset deletions are never recorded. Scheduled-settings history is written but not shown in the panel. A failed history write fails the user's project save and scheduled-settings save. Every saved .3mf embeds history by default with no opt-in. The identity-history panel filters only the current 10-row page with ISO text dates, and most of its strings are missing from the yue_HK catalogue.

## exports

A strong wx-free export engine is in place: 17 formats with per-datum loss reports, UTF-8 output with selectable line endings and schema headers, ZIP via miniz, and a full 7-Zip option surface with encrypted headers and path sanitizing. A shared ExportDialog with an Open in VS Code action sits on top. Only nine surfaces route through it: preset, object list, print statistics, preferences, notification history, project history list, changelog (prose only), and redacted local-security text. Several other surfaces write bespoke single-format files (multi-machine, config profiles, workspace checklist, converter CSV, Ollama session JSON, appearance theme JSON). Many owned lists have no export at all: calibration history, Helio history, scheduled rules, settings drafts, saved searches, docs articles, command palette, model creator revisions, and the embedded filament-manager and recent-files pages. No exported dataset can be re-imported. The preferences and preset exports are allowlisted partial exports with no complete, sensitivity-marked path. The docs contradict the code in places, and the newer exports README has no Cantonese twin.

## changelog

Help > What's new / Changelog and the About dialog both open a native changelog viewer. It shows releases newest-first with date, tag, code names, categorized entries, full-SHA commit links, and an honest note for empty releases. It has a typed-date filter that reads the locale order and ISO, keeps invalid input and reports it inline, plus an anchored calendar with month/year jump, range and presets. Search uses the shared regex builder, copy and export honour the filters and keep full SHAs, and entries appear in English, Cantonese or both. The bundled data is stale: 170 releases, newest md3-v164 generated 2026-09-29, while 63 later numbered tags (md3-v165 to md3-v227) and about 800 commits are missing. SHA validation runs only when the exporter is invoked, not at build time. Entries are not styled by the funny-level sliders. Entries cannot be selected, so copying a selection is impossible. Export is prose only, which serializes poorly to structured formats. The commit-link forge is hard-coded rather than taken from build provenance.

## external-editor

Three parts of the general capability work: editor detection (registry plus PATH for VS Code, Insiders, VSCodium, Sublime, Notepad++, Cursor, Windsurf and Zed), a persisted Preferences choice with a Custom executable path, and File > Open in External Editor, which opens the current project folder and shows a toast when no editor is configured. The shared ExportDialog adds a dedicated Open in VS Code action. It opens folders as a new-window workspace root, never substitutes another editor, and offers Download VS Code when Code is missing. Several parts are missing. There is no way to open a selected file. Only exports that go through ExportDialog get the VS Code handoff; G-code, 3MF and STL exports, bulk exports, backups and bespoke exports do not, and no record offers it either. Portable VS Code is detected only when it is on PATH, with no manual locate option. Detection is cached per process. The VS Code strings are missing from the Cantonese catalogue, and there are no tests.

## notifications

Audited at main HEAD 45b0a9ec9. That is two commits after 38c76dfdf, and both touch only the README screenshot workflow and the documentation bundle. The native canvas toasts (NotificationManager) stack bottom-up in the bottom-right corner of the 3D/Preview/Assemble GL canvas. Regular toasts fade after 10 s. Errors and warnings persist until dismissed. Hyperlink and second-action callbacks work. A bell-and-popover notification centre has a searchable, exportable, persisted history with tests. show_info, warning_catcher and show_error now route to toasts. The contract is still broken in several places. (1) The funnels fall back to a MODAL dialog whenever any modal dialog is open or before the Plater exists. (2) Toasts render only on the GL canvas, so messages raised while the Home, Device, Project or Calibration tab is active cannot be seen. (3) At least 233 OK-only MessageDialog sites, 27 wxMessageBox calls and the device/update InfoDialog paths bypass the funnels. These include GUI_App::push_notification, EVT_SHOW_DIALOG and the 'This is the newest version.' InfoDialog. (4) Toasts have no separate title field; the funnel builds 'title: message'. (5) ImGui toasts are not announced to screen readers. (6) The embedded Home page still calls a blocking debug alert(), and the web toast styling ships only with the model editor page. (7) The source regression covers only about 8 call sites. (8) The notification-centre filter rows cannot be collapsed. (9) Two notification articles lack Cantonese twins. The Pages documentation site (ui-md3/site) has a compliant toast system.

## progress-recovery

A few dialogs follow the contract. The shared ExportDialog shows phase progress, disables its controls, refuses re-entry while an export runs and can cancel. The send-print and send-to-SD dialogs disable Send, guard with m_is_in_sending_mode and show an in-dialog status bar. The converter, Smart Home and Model Creator use running/in-flight flags. Cloud web pages show a non-modal failure bar with Retry, and project-history failures carry a retry link. There is no shared long-operation guard and no per-surface source test. Many dialog-started operations break the contract. PhysicalPrinterDialog runs its host connection test and printer refresh as blocking UI-thread network calls behind a busy cursor. Model Creator shows only a status sentence while it generates. A manual update check runs Update.exe with no progress beyond one 'Downloading in the background' toast. Model import from a URL uses an app-modal percent-only ProgressDialog. The Ollama batch pull button is wired to a no-op. No dialog offers a choice to skip an expensive optional phase. Refused credentials never offer re-authentication directly: an expired cloud login logs the user out and shows a modal OK dialog, and the cloud web failure bar offers only Retry. Nothing hands a failure to a local coding agent, even though the app already launches Claude Code CLI and Codex CLI for Model Creator. The integration inventory marks these rows Incomplete.

## download-handoff

The repository has no browser extension, no native-messaging host and no download-capture surfaces. The closest existing route comes from upstream: the bambustudio://open URL scheme, a macOS bambustudioopen:// URL and the embedded MakerWorld 'makerworld_model_open' command all call request_model_download. Plater::import_model_id then starts the transfer at once. No Start download dialog names the file, source and destination; the only gate is a modal YES/NO prompt for untrusted hosts. Progress shows in an app-modal ProgressDialog with a percentage only: no bytes, rate, ETA, pause or resume, and no separate window. There is no completion surface, because the app simply opens the project. This fork also never registers the URL protocol: the NSIS installer and GUI_App::associate_files register file extensions only, so even the legacy browser handoff probably cannot reach an installed copy. No documentation, localization, tests or captures exist. A Windows desktop app can host an extension handoff, so this family cannot be marked not-applicable.

## forge-publishing

Nothing in the app publishes a repository to a forge. The only publish flow is upstream 'Publish to MakerWorld' (PublishDialog). It uses the single Bambu cloud account held by the closed network plug-in, with no account or owner choice and no multi-account store. Project version history is already a libgit2 repository per project, but it is local-only and has no remotes. A forge-publish surface is therefore feasible: libgit2, HTTP and Windows Credential Manager wrappers already exist. This family is missing, not not-applicable. This family also covers the 'provider-authored text is rendered' section, because forge-authored text is its main source. That section is not met either. The GitHub release body for app updates is printed as a plain wxLabel. A URL pulled out of a release body can load in an in-app WebView created with the app's 'wx' script bridge. Firmware and plug-in notes are printed as labels. There are two separate Markdown renderers: libslic3r Markdown for the documentation browser and a bundled JS renderer in resources/tooltip. Neither has an emoji shortcode map or an accessible region label, and neither renders an honest empty state for provider text.

## file-converter

Audited at HEAD 45b0a9ec9. That is two commits after 38c76dfd, and those commits only add a screenshot workflow and regenerate the docs bundle, so no converter code changed. The native converter has a strong core. It has a documented registry covering all eight required categories. Adapters stay disabled until the bundled worker passes a SHA-256 check and a live capability probe, and unavailable formats (extended images, audio, video, multi-entry archives, office, DOCX/EPUB) stay visible with exact reasons. Conversions run in a zero-capability AppContainer worker under a job object (one process, 256 MiB, 30 s) with no PATH, shell or network. Every output is validated before an atomic no-replace publish that re-reads the source. Seven qpdf 12.4.2 PDF operations are hash-pinned, and the durable paged queue has no total cap, persistent pause/resume/cancel, crash-to-recovery-required handling and a storage preflight. The panel is reachable from File > Local file converter in the Local tools tab. The user-facing surface falls short of the contract in several ways. It is built from raw wx controls (wxNotebook, wxListCtrl, wxTextCtrl) rather than registered MD3 primitives. It has no Cantonese or bilingual translations, and adapter names, disclosures, reasons, states and result codes are untranslatable English from libslic3r. Lossy changes are disclosed but never explicitly acknowledged. The only preview is a kind-and-byte-count status line. Bulk actions cover only the current page. The PDF metadata tool edits only Title. There is no open-output or editor action, no notification integration and no funny levels. PDF is known to fail initialization inside the AppContainer (USER32 1114) in the verification context. No focused test runs in CI. The Pages site and the embedded web pages have no converter surface. Audio and Video have no enabled adapters; they are honestly disabled, which meets the letter of the contract but leaves those categories with no working conversion.

## ollama-suite

No longer missing (the old inventory was stale). The bounded core is real: an allowlisted local API client on a fixed 127.0.0.1:11434 with no proxy or redirects, and bounded JSON/NDJSON parsing. Capabilities come from /api/show. Exact manifest sizes come from the official registry. There is a catalog traversal with a completeness flag, a durable pull queue and a reviewed PullBatch engine with 1-4 workers, a chat store with redacted export, and typed launch profiles with preflight, snapshot and rollback. A modal dialog (File > Local model suite) uses a shared TabStrip with Models, Chat, Batch pulls, Launch profiles and Troubleshooting. Much of the contract is still unmet. Batch pull start is a permanently disabled no-op, and PullBatch is never called by the UI. Hardware detection supplies only RAM and architecture, and every call site passes no context overhead and discards free disk. As a result every fit verdict in the real app is Unknown, and harness launch preflight is always blocked. The HTML catalog never sets authority_total_known, so the catalog is never written to catalog.json and no last verified catalog exists offline. The Model Store has text search only, with no filters, grouping or sorting. There is no delete or copy UI. Chat has three parameters, applies the system prompt only to the first message, has no retry/regenerate, searches sessions on the current page only, and its export omits all message text. The troubleshooter is static text that says installation and start are unavailable, with no bundled-help link. Profile registration and persistence, Ollama configuration snapshots and vault-backed secrets are missing. Worker status strings are raw English, and no suite string has a yue_HK translation. The dialog is modal and not registered with SurfaceRegistry. There is no notification integration, no Pages site or embedded-page equivalent, no CI test run, and no Cantonese article twin.

## offline-docs

There are two separate in-app documentation browsers, and each satisfies a different part of the contract. DocsBrowserDialog is opened from F1 and Help > Documentation. It reads a bundle.json that BundleDocs.cmake generates at build time from every docs/features article and renders it with the shared libslic3r Markdown renderer in WebView2. It resolves article links in-app through bambudocs://, searches titles and bodies with the shared SearchField regex builder, and selects Cantonese companions in Cantonese mode. Documentation::OfflineDocumentation is opened from Help > Offline documentation and from every command-palette Documentation row. It uses a checked-in DocumentationBundle.hpp (363 articles) that was pre-rendered by a second, Python-side renderer in scripts/documentation/build_bundle.py. It adds an EN/Cantonese/bilingual selector, article tabs and multi-select copy/export. This breaks the one-shared-renderer rule. Neither path has a build-failing completeness guard. BundleDocs.cmake only globs and writes: a missing title becomes an empty title and a missing image only warns. build_bundle.py --check passes at HEAD, but no CMake target or workflow runs it, and the Python and native bundle tests are not in CI. The shared Markdown renderer has no unit tests. 27 relative .md links in feature articles point at repository docs outside docs/features and open a browser or show as unavailable. 31 English feature articles have no .yue_HK.md twin, bilingual mode in DocsBrowserDialog shows English only, and some OfflineDocumentation strings are untranslated. documentation-browser.md says the palette opens DocsBrowserDialog, which contradicts the code.

## landing-and-docs-site

A Material 3 tabbed GitHub Pages site exists. ## line-count

A committed counter, scripts/ci/Measure-LineCount.ps1, runs in the release workflow, and its table goes into every release's notes. It separates source, tests, styles/markup/docs, generated and excluded rows. It reports total and non-blank lines, attributes surviving lines with git blame, checks its own arithmetic, and states its exclusions. Gaps remain. Agent attribution uses only the blamed author name, so about 200 maintainer and test-identity commits that carry Co-Authored-By trailers naming an agent count as other. Generated detection matches only path segments, so large generated files count as hand-written: changelog.data.js, DocumentationBundle.hpp and BambuStudio.pot. There is no per-language or per-subproject split. The notes do not record the exact command line. The counter has no test and no article. Spot-check results. Confirmed: logo-customization is missing (src/slic3r/GUI/AppLogo/LogoPanel.cpp is in no CMake list and is referenced nowhere; only libslic3r/AppLogo/Logo.hpp and an unregistered tests/app_logo exist). unlock-ladder is missing (no ladder code anywhere). download-handoff is missing (no extension or native messaging host; DownloadProgressDialog is the upstream plug-in download dialog). sanitized-instruction-copy is missing (AGENTS.md is 30 lines with no mirror). offline-docs has exactly 31 missing Cantonese twins (197 English, 166 twins). (1) The dim sum default mismatch blocks the build on the audited main: commit 29b64dafd (2026-10-05) set LanguageMode.hpp:77 to 5, DimSumSurpriseModel.hpp:377 is still 2, and DimSumSurprise.cpp:5 static_asserts that they are equal. That file is compiled (src/slic3r/CMakeLists.txt:900), so 38c76dfd and HEAD 45b0a9ec cannot compile. The README's 'exact-main root build at cc059003d passed' claim predates 29b64dafd. (2) collapse-filters should be partial, not missing: the G-code legend has a user fold toggle. (3) adhd-modes is missing in the native app: PersonalModes/AttentionModes.hpp is not included by any compiled source and Preferences has no attention controls; only the Pages site implements the modes. (4) forge-publishing needs a recorded applicability decision: the app has no repository-publishing flow (PublishDialog.cpp is MakerWorld publishing).
